jobs.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a new wide fantasy lore-card painting in the detailed painterly style and grizzly identity of the reference. In a dense ancient forest, a huge russet grizzly stands on its hind legs delivering a devastating sweeping paw strike. Two armored adult soldiers are visibly thrown through the air by the swipe, their bodies recoiling with believable weight; three defeated adult soldiers lie motionless nearby with dropped shields and spears. No gore or dismemberment. The bear is the dominant central figure, with massive shoulders, long claws and a small ember-red ancient branching rune on its brow. Dynamic clear silhouettes, green forest depths and warm shafts of light, crisp rich fur detail. Frame the full upright bear, airborne soldiers and fallen soldiers within the composition. No writing, captions, UI, border or watermark. Landscape image.

jobs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW four-frame death animation sprite sheet for the exact bulky russet grizzly identity and crisp painterly fur style of the reference. Four complete whole-bear paintings in a spacious 2 by 2 grid, equal cells, read left to right then top to bottom. All four paintings keep the SAME front-right three-quarter view, muzzle points down-right with no camera turning and consistent body size. Frame1: wounded bear on four legs, head sagging and front knees starting to buckle. Frame2: forequarters drop, both front elbows fold with chest nearly grounded and hindquarters still high. Frame3: the heavy body rolls onto its flank, hind legs folding, muzzle near ground. Frame4: fully dead and motionless on its side, torso and head resting on ground, all four paws anatomically correct, closed eyes, no breathing pose. This is a weighty collapse, no gore or wounds. Preserve complete ears, muzzle, all paws and fur in every cell; generous margins and separation, no touching figures. Transparent PNG with actual alpha channel, no checkerboard, no ground plane, no background, no shadows, no text, no numbers. Do not reuse standing poses for the final death frames.
